parsed.attack: Capture is daily, payoff is monthly, and the payoff lands on somebody else's screen, so the incentive is upside down for the person doing the tapping. What actually happens by week two is the shoebox: receipts pile up on the counter unphotographed and get done in one batch on the 30th, which means the month-end session the product promised to abolish still exists, only now with a camera in it - and a user who has discovered batching works does not open the app for twenty-nine days out of thirty. The medical-POA sibling, who has no account and no duty to the numbers, opens the statement once out of politeness and then stops, removing the only witness the record had.
parsed.strongest_defence: A fiduciary accounting duty does not lapse and elder care runs two to seven years, so the monthly trigger arrives whether or not anyone enjoys it, and even batched camera capture is many times faster than re-keying a stack of receipts into Excel - the retained value is the statement, not the daily habit, and the statement is needed every single month. The accumulated record is legally load-bearing, which makes cancelling costly in a way a productivity app's history never is.
parsed.verdict_reason: The monthly duty is a genuine recurring trigger with a defendable record, but the daily capture loop collapses into a month-end batch by week two and the second sibling stops opening the statement.
